card.title: Portfolio
card.tagline: The site you're on right now
card.summary: Designed and built end to end: bilingual, dressed in a hand-made paper aesthetic, with transitions that stitch every section together like a notebook.

hero.title: Portfolio
hero.tagline: A bilingual site with a paper texture, built to feel hand-made.

overview.tools: Next.js · Tailwind · Framer Motion · Claude Code (MCP)

problem.heading: A portfolio that didn't feel like a template.
problem.body: I wanted a site that spoke about me in two languages without either one feeling 'translated,' and that looked and felt hand-made — more scrapbook than corporate landing page. The hard part wasn't technical: it was making every section, from the hero to the contact form, breathe the same paper warmth without sacrificing accessibility or performance.

research.heading: Setting the tone before the code.
research.body: I started with the content: I reviewed every string in Spanish and English so translations were contextual Latin American Spanish, not literal copies of the English. From there came the visual direction — aged paper, torn edges, washi tape as an accent — and the modular structure it would need to grow: projects, photography and art, all fed by JSON instead of hardcoded copy.

process.heading: From design system to the details no one asks for.
process.body: I built a warm color system (sage, terracotta, cream) checked against WCAG AA contrast, and a shared paper-texture layer used across the whole app: torn edges generated from Catmull-Rom splines over SVG filters, decorative washi tape, and a portrait card with an irregular deckle edge. Projects, photography and art all live in modular JSON — adding a new piece never touches component code. Transitions between sections use Framer Motion and the View Transitions API so a card on the homepage literally morphs into the hero of its destination page. I closed the loop with a working contact form via Resend, a CV download, a custom Open Graph image, a sitemap, and a full accessibility and performance pass.
flows: Home — hero, projects and 'Beyond the work'
Photography and art — standalone pages, tied back to the home

flowGroups.title: The home page
flows: Hero — torn-edge portrait with a CV download CTA
Projects — cards with a shared transition into each case study
Beyond the work — photography and art as clippings pinned with washi tape
notes: The portrait reuses the same torn-edge clip-path as the art cards — visual consistency without duplicating code.
Each project card carries its own viewTransitionName; clicking it, the card becomes the case study's hero.
The two 'photos' in this block sit at a slight tilt, connected by a hand-drawn SVG thread, like a corkboard of references.

flowGroups.title: Photography and art, as their own pages
flows: Photography — a mosaic of images with a paper mount and a slight tilt
Art — a piece-by-piece viewer with the story and materials behind each one
notes: Every photo gets its own paper margin and a subtle random tilt, so the mosaic never reads as a perfect grid.
In Art, switching pieces triggers a directional Framer Motion transition — the image, the background tint and the label slide together with no layout jump, no matter the artwork's size.

results.heading: A site that feels finished in the details.
results.body: The result is a complete bilingual portfolio — home, projects, photography, art and a working contact form — where the paper texture, transitions and copy feel like one object, not stacked layers. It passes AA contrast, respects prefers-reduced-motion, is fully keyboard-navigable, and generates its own Open Graph image.
learnings: Designing the texture system (paper, torn edges, washi tape) as reusable components from the start kept every new section from feeling bolted on.
Splitting content into per-language JSON — even for new sections like photography and art — made it trivial to swap in real pieces later without touching components.
Shared transitions (View Transitions + Framer Motion) do more to sell the feeling of 'one place' than any single animation on its own.

reflection.heading: What I'm taking with me.
reflection.body: This site is, in itself, the project that best sums up how I work: define the system before the screens, care about the detail no one asked for (the grain of the paper, the correct translation, the contrast of a secondary label), and build with AI tools like Claude Code without ever skipping a hand review of each decision.
